results.reason: The response says the Varga acquisition is a Change of Control under DA 1.1 that requires Crestline's prior written consent under DA 15.4. It says Part 3.5 of the Disclosure Schedule wrongly lists the agreement as notice only. It explains the resulting termination right, termination fee, and inaccurate consents representation.

Issue 2 says DA 14.2, read with the 1.1 'Qualified Transferee' definition, lets Crestline assign without consent to any lab or diagnostic distributor in the Territory. It notes the definition does not exclude competitors or their affiliates.

Issue 3 says First Amendment Section 3.1 restates 12.3 so that only Section 9 breaches are carved out, dropping the Section 10 and Section 11 carve-outs. It says the amendment controls under DA 17.5, so those claims are now capped.
The response states that the original 12.3 excluded breaches of Section 9, breaches of Section 10, and indemnification obligations under Section 11.
The response states that the DA 12.2 cap equals the amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The response is a memo with the issues listed separately. Each issue has headings for document/section, why it matters for Halvorsen, and a recommended fix.
The response expressly concludes that Crestline's consent is required and that the notice-only description is wrong.
The response expressly says the original carve-outs no longer apply.
